analysis.one_liner: Shriram Finance is India's largest non-bank lender (NBFC), built on financing used and new commercial vehicles, with gold loans, MSME and personal loans as newer additions.
analysis.whats_happening: Q1 FY27 results (June 2026 quarter, reported 24 Jul 2026) showed standalone PAT of ₹3,444.56 cr, up roughly 60% YoY, with net interest income up 33.7% YoY to ₹8,055.70 cr and total AUM crossing ₹3.14 lakh crore (+15.26% YoY). In April 2026, Japan's MUFG Bank completed a ₹39,618 cr preferential share allotment for a 20.02% stake, and CRISIL, ICRA and India Ratings upgraded the company's long-term credit rating to AAA. Q2 FY27 results are expected around mid-November 2026, based on last year's reporting pattern, but the exact date is not yet confirmed - check the exchange filing nearer the time.
analysis.plain_terms: This company lends money for trucks and used commercial vehicles - a segment banks mostly avoid - and has layered on gold loans and small-business lending. Profit and interest income both grew fast this quarter, helped by lending margins widening to 9.04% from 8.11% a year ago. But bad loans (GNPA) crept up slightly to 4.64% from 4.58% in the prior quarter, so the growth hasn't been entirely free of cost - that's the tension to watch rather than take the headline profit growth at face value.
analysis.quarters: Q1 FY27 (Jun-2026): PAT ₹3,444.56 cr (+~60% YoY), NII ₹8,055.70 cr (+33.7% YoY), AUM ₹3,13,798 cr (+15.26% YoY, CV AUM alone +47% YoY to ₹1.47 lakh cr), NIM 9.04% (up from 8.61% in Q4 FY26), GNPA 4.64% (up from 4.58%), NNPA 2.33% (flat), credit cost 1.66% of total assets. This follows Q4 FY26 (Mar-2026): PAT ₹3,013-3,021 cr (+41% YoY), AUM past ₹3 lakh cr for the first time, GNPA 4.58%. Management reaffirmed FY27 AUM growth guidance of ~18% (floor of ~15%) and credit cost guidance near 2%, said NIM should hold close to 9% for a couple more quarters before easing toward ~8.5% as the mix shifts toward new-vehicle financing, and did not flag the GNPA uptick as a concern on the call.
analysis.performance_read: Returns have been exceptional across every horizon shown: +41.4% over 1 year versus Nifty's -9.5%, +160.9% over 3 years versus Nifty's +16.8%, and +268% over 5 years versus Nifty's +25.3% - comfortably ahead of peer CHOLAFIN at every horizon too. The stock did a 5:1 split in January 2025; that is a share-count adjustment, not a demerger, so it does not distort the long-run return figures the way a spin-off would. More recently the stock is down 17.6% from its 6 August 2026 peak of ₹1,141 and has underperformed the Nifty over the last 3 months (-9.2% vs -4.9%), though it remains well above its 52-week low of ₹664.67.
analysis.valuation_read: At ₹939.95, the stock trades near 19.4-19.5x trailing earnings and about 2.7x book value (book value ~₹350/share). That is not statistically cheap for a vehicle-finance NBFC - it is priced for continued high-teens AUM growth, a return on assets near 4%, and the credibility boost from the AAA rating upgrade and MUFG's large capital infusion. Whether that premium is justified depends on GNPA staying contained and NIM not compressing faster than management's own guidance.
analysis.growth_read: Growth is currently both volume- and margin-led: AUM is up 15.3% YoY (core commercial-vehicle AUM up 47% YoY) while NIM has also expanded nearly a full percentage point YoY to 9.04%. Management itself guides NIM to ease back toward ~8.5% over the medium term as the loan mix shifts toward lower-margin new-vehicle financing, which would make future growth progressively more volume-dependent and less margin-assisted than it has been this quarter.
analysis.health_read: Profitability metrics look solid - ROA of 3.93% and credit cost of 1.66% of assets - and the AAA rating upgrade plus a ₹2,220 cr NCD raise in September 2026 at a 7.80% coupon suggest comfortable access to funding. As a lending business, leverage is structural rather than a red flag by itself, but the debt-to-equity figure could not be pinned down precisely (sources ranged from 2.76x to 3.87x) - Not verified, check on Screener or the latest investor presentation. The more relevant risk here is business risk - whether used-vehicle and gold-loan asset quality holds up (GNPA 4.64%, drifting up) - rather than a financial or liquidity risk, which currently looks well managed.
analysis.ownership_read: Promoter holding fell to roughly 20.30% from 25.38% in the prior quarter - this is dilution from MUFG Bank's ₹39,618 cr preferential share allotment completed in April 2026 for a 20.02% stake (with two board seats and a three-year promoter lock-up), not a promoter sale. Pledging stands at 0%. FII holding jumped to ~54.75%, largely because MUFG's new shares are classified as FII; DIIs hold ~19.9%, including Norway's sovereign wealth fund (1.23%) and domestic mutual funds such as SBI, Kotak and Motilal Oswal (roughly 1.4-1.7% each). No well-known individual investor is visible on the public register.
strengths: NII grew 33.7% YoY to ₹8,055.70 cr in Q1 FY27 as NIM expanded to 9.04% from 8.11% a year earlier
Core commercial-vehicle AUM, the company's traditional strength, grew 47% YoY to ₹1.47 lakh crore
Credit rating upgraded to AAA by CRISIL, ICRA and India Ratings in April 2026, alongside a large capital infusion from MUFG Bank
watchpoints: GNPA rose to 4.64% from 4.58% quarter-on-quarter even as management maintained an unconcerned tone - worth tracking whether this is a blip or a trend
Reported ROE figures conflict sharply across sources (16.4% TTM on Screener versus 18.5%/20.9% cited elsewhere) - the precise number needs verification against the company's own filing
Debt-to-equity/leverage ratio could not be independently confirmed (range cited: 2.76x-3.87x) - Not verified, check on Screener
Management itself guides NIM to compress from the current 9.04% toward ~8.5% over the medium term as the lending mix shifts toward lower-margin new-vehicle financing
analysis.one_thing: Whether GNPA (4.64% in Q1 FY27, up from 4.58%) stabilizes or keeps climbing over the next one to two quarters will show whether the current profit and margin growth is durable or is being achieved alongside quietly deteriorating asset quality.
analysis.data_notes: Price, return, dividend and split data taken as supplied and treated as verified. Q1 FY27 and Q4 FY26 PAT/NII/AUM/NIM/GNPA figures were cross-checked across Business Standard, Free Press Journal, ScanX and an NSE call transcript and were consistent. ROE/ROA figures and the debt-to-equity ratio conflicted across sources and were not reconciled - flagged explicitly rather than averaged, per policy. The MUFG stake and AAA rating upgrade were corroborated across multiple sources. The Q2 FY27 results date is an inference from last year's calendar, not a confirmed figure.
